blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.2
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.2

blocks.text: ज्ञानं बन्धः
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानं बन्धः

blocks.text: Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ.
blocks.directed: Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ.

blocks.text: Knowledge is bondage.
blocks.directed: Knowledge is bondage.

blocks.text: Congratulations, Your Knowledge Is the Problem.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, Your Knowledge Is the Problem.

blocks.text: Oh, brilliant.
blocks.directed: Oh, brilliant.

blocks.text: We’ve gone from “you are infinite consciousness” to “knowledge is your prison”.
blocks.directed: We’ve gone from “you are infinite consciousness” to “knowledge is your prison”.

blocks.text: Thanks, Vasugupta. Shall I cancel university?
blocks.directed: Thanks, Vasugupta. Shall I cancel university?

blocks.text: Not quite.
blocks.directed: Not quite.

blocks.text: Here jñāna means limited, differentiated knowing — knowledge structured around the fundamental division:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Here jñāna means limited, differentiated knowing — knowledge structured around the fundamental division:

blocks.text: I am here. That thing is over there.
blocks.directed: I am here. That thing is over there.

blocks.text: You see a tree.
blocks.directed: You see a tree.

blocks.text: There is you, the perceiver, and the tree, the perceived.
blocks.directed: There is you, the perceiver, and the tree, the perceived.

blocks.text: You immediately organise reality into categories.
blocks.directed: You immediately organise reality into categories.

blocks.text: Me. Tree. Other people. My possessions. My memories. My terribly important opinions.
blocks.directed: Me. Tree. Other people. My possessions. My memories. My terribly important opinions.

blocks.text: Now ordinary differentiated knowledge is useful. It stops you walking into trees.
blocks.directed: Now ordinary differentiated knowledge is useful. It stops you walking into trees.

blocks.text: But the problem begins when this limited standpoint is mistaken for your complete identity.
blocks.directed: But the problem begins when this limited standpoint is mistaken for your complete identity.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja associates this with āṇavamala, the primordial contraction in which universal consciousness experiences itself as a limited individual.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja associates this with āṇavamala, the primordial contraction in which universal consciousness experiences itself as a limited individual.

blocks.text: Mala means impurity, but don’t imagine literal dirt covering a perfectly clean soul.
blocks.directed: Mala means impurity, but don’t imagine literal dirt covering a perfectly clean soul.

blocks.text: Think of it as a fundamental limitation of awareness.
blocks.directed: Think of it as a fundamental limitation of awareness.

blocks.text: The infinite experiences itself as finite.
blocks.directed: The infinite experiences itself as finite.

blocks.text: The complete experiences itself as incomplete.
blocks.directed: The complete experiences itself as incomplete.

blocks.text: The universally free experiences itself as somebody who desperately needs everything to work out a particular way.
blocks.directed: The universally free experiences itself as somebody who desperately needs everything to work out a particular way.

blocks.text: And here’s the extraordinary move.
blocks.directed: And here’s the extraordinary move.

blocks.text: From the Trika perspective, bondage doesn’t require a second power to capture Śiva.
blocks.directed: From the Trika perspective, bondage doesn’t require a second power to capture Śiva.

blocks.text: Śiva’s own freedom makes contraction possible.
blocks.directed: Śiva’s own freedom makes contraction possible.

blocks.text: The prisoner, the prison, and the authority permitting the imprisonment are not ultimately three independent entities.
blocks.directed: The prisoner, the prison, and the authority permitting the imprisonment are not ultimately three independent entities.

blocks.text: It’s Śiva.
blocks.directed: It’s Śiva.

blocks.text: Doing the entire performance himself.
blocks.directed: Doing the entire performance himself.

blocks.text: The philosophical point: Bondage is not knowledge as such, but the limiting mode of knowing which obscures one’s undivided nature. Kṣemarāja also connects bondage to the failure to recognise nondual awareness.
blocks.directed: The philosophical point: Bondage is not knowledge as such, but the limiting mode of knowing which obscures one’s undivided nature. Kṣemarāja also connects bondage to the failure to recognise nondual awareness.
